facts.value: Level B2 (CEFR) or equivalent in written and spoken English and German. Honours undergraduate degree (Level 8 NFQ or equivalent) at 2.1 or higher (or equivalent), with a major/minor specialization in Linguistics, German, English, Journalism or related fields.

MA-level degree (Level 9 NFQ or equivalent) in Applied Linguistics/Sociolinguistics, Journalism, Sociology/Social Sciences or related fields, openness to interdisciplinary methods and some experience in qualitative and quantitative methods, some knowledge of/experience in discourse analysis and/or linguistic corpus analysis.
Include a cover letter (max. 1000 words), a curriculum vitae, a writing sample, contact details of two academic referees, and transcripts of university-level grades.
Interviews for the position will be held online in September 2026.
Fee waivers are open to incoming and current research postgraduate students, unless otherwise stated. Current students must be in good academic standing.
Prospective PhD students are encouraged to apply and need not have completed an application for acceptance onto an AHSS research postgraduate programme before doing so.
New applicants must formally register for an AHSS PhD programme by 1 September 2026 if awarded a fee waiver.
Applicants must submit a completed application form and one academic reference to Ann-Marie Hickey by the closing date.
